question: When does a compositional or split neural architecture actually cause its modules to specialize in distinct input-output mappings, and when does modularity fail to produce systematic generalization?

key_findings.claim: The paper formalizes systematic generalization as learning low-rank compositional submappings from an incomplete partition of a parameterized dataset space.
key_findings.evidence: Inputs and outputs are decomposed into structured and nuisance components, and held-out combinations test whether the learner recovers reusable mappings rather than interpolating a higher-rank aggregate relation.

key_findings.claim: Linear gradient dynamics show that module specialization is not guaranteed by merely placing several modules in the architecture.
key_findings.evidence: The derived mode dynamics depend on how data partitions expose component mappings and how those mappings are assigned to modules. Without a sufficiently aligned partition or inductive bias, modules can learn entangled mixtures that fit training combinations but fail systematically held-out ones.

key_findings.claim: A dense network generally cannot be expected to select the intended systematic mapping when multiple training-consistent extensions exist.
key_findings.evidence: The theoretical construction exhibits full-data solutions that differ on the missing combination, and the learned extension follows implicit bias and data geometry rather than a generic principle of compositionality.

anchors.section: Rank of compositional and noncompositional mappings

key_findings.claim: A split CNN improves held-out compositional-digit performance when its channel partition matches the generative factors, but imperfect partitions degrade the advantage.
key_findings.evidence: On the compositional MNIST construction, two parallel convolutional streams with controlled routing systematically generalize better than a comparable dense CNN. Appendix analyses and experiments vary imperfect output partitions and show specialization is sensitive to alignment.

method.core_idea: Analyze modular specialization through the joint geometry of dataset partitions, low-rank input-output mappings, and gradient-descent dynamics rather than treating modularity as an architectural label.
method.mechanism: A parametric matrix dataset exposes or withholds combinations of component factors. Exact linear-network dynamics decompose learning into modes associated with possible mappings; alternative module/data assignments predict specialization or entanglement. A split-versus-dense CNN experiment instantiates the mechanism with composed MNIST factors.
assumptions: Linear-network dynamics reveal mechanisms relevant to nonlinear convolutional modules.
The synthetic dataset factorization corresponds to the intended reusable subproblems.
Systematic generalization is adequately measured by one held-out cross-product partition.
Module routing or output partition information is available and meaningfully aligned with the factors.

techniques.role: Makes training and held-out compositional structure algebraically explicit.
Tracks which candidate mappings are learned and at what rates.
Separates low-rank compositional maps from higher-rank shortcut extensions.
Imposes a module partition aligned with distinct generative factors in the nonlinear test.

evaluations.setting: Analytically tractable linear modular and dense networks on parameterized compositional matrix datasets.
evaluations.metric: Training dynamics of mapping coefficients and error on a held-out factor combination.
evaluations.result: Specialization emerges only in selected data/module partitions; otherwise training-consistent entangled maps dominate or coexist.
evaluations.baseline: Dense linear learning and alternative module assignment structures.

evaluations.setting: Compositional MNIST with a held-out combination of digit-derived factors.
evaluations.metric: Accuracy/generalization error on observed and systematic holdout partitions.
evaluations.result: The aligned split CNN preserves training performance while improving the unseen combination relative to the dense CNN.

evaluations.setting: Imperfect output partitions and architecture/hyperparameter controls.
evaluations.metric: Change in specialization and held-out performance as alignment is corrupted.
evaluations.result: The benefit weakens when the imposed split no longer matches the true factors, reinforcing the data-architecture co-design claim.

limitations: The exact theory concerns linear networks and stylized matrix datasets.
The nonlinear evidence is a small synthetic digit-composition task rather than natural multimodal or language reasoning.
The best-performing split receives prior knowledge about the relevant factor partition.
Alternative mechanisms such as routing, sparsity, attention, and learned module assignment are not studied at modern scale.
failure_modes: Modules specialize to nuisance partitions if the training distribution correlates nuisance with intended factors.
A rigid split can prevent useful information sharing when factors are not independent.
Dense models may fit observed combinations with a non-systematic extension that is indistinguishable on training loss.
Learned routing can collapse several factors into one module without explicit diversity pressure.
reusable_insights: Modularity should be evaluated as an interaction between data partition, routing, and optimizer bias.
Held-out Cartesian-product combinations are necessary to distinguish fitting from systematic reuse.
Rank and singular-mode analysis can expose multiple training-equivalent but extrapolatively different solutions.
open_questions: Can module partitions be learned from weak interventions without supplying the factor labels?
How do the specialization conditions change for nonlinear attention and mixture-of-experts routing?
What diagnostics detect entangled modules before an expensive held-out systematicity test?

competitive_landscape.title: How Modular Should Neural Module Networks Be for Systematic Generalization?
competitive_landscape.relationship: Empirically varies the degree and location of modularity in neural module networks across compositional VQA datasets.
competitive_landscape.difference: It searches architectural modularity empirically; this paper derives specialization dynamics from dataset/mapping geometry and tests an aligned split CNN.

competitive_landscape.title: Neural Module Networks for Reasoning over Text
competitive_landscape.relationship: Builds executable learned modules for discrete compositional operations over text and shows the importance of intermediate supervision.
competitive_landscape.difference: It engineers task-semantic modules for DROP; this paper asks more fundamentally when generic modules become specialized under gradient training.

competitive_landscape.title: Improving Compositionality of Neural Networks by Decoding Representations to Inputs
competitive_landscape.relationship: Adds a decoding constraint to make neural components more composable and auditable.
competitive_landscape.difference: It enforces representation-level decodability; this work analyzes specialization of mappings across modules and identifies when data partitions supply the needed inductive bias.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The work supplies a dynamical theory of neural-module specialization and shows that data partition and modular architecture must align for systematic generalization.
novelty_assessment.evidence: Exact linear mode dynamics predict multiple specialization regimes, and the aligned split-versus-dense CNN experiment qualitatively validates them.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The data-architecture coupling is an important corrective to vague modularity claims; generalization to learned routers and realistic tasks remains the central missing test.

reviewer_notes: Read the 31-page ICLR manuscript including imperfect-partition proofs and CMNIST details. Direct modularity/compositionality work was checked at primary arXiv records on 2026-08-23.
